subject: DPA question: training consent, subprocessors, and EU transfer routing
messages:
From: Olivia Park <olivia.park@clinicahealth.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: James Turner <j.turner@clinicahealth.com>, Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@hjl-law.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 14:12:00 +0000
Subject: DPA: clarification on training consent, subprocessors and EU routing

Hi Markus —

Thanks for the demo last week. Legal and engineering dug into the draft DPA and had a couple of items we need clarified before we move to signature:

1) Training / model improvement: the draft currently references "customer data may be used to improve models". ClinicaHealth requires an explicit no-training commitment for PHI-adjacent prompts unless we opt in. Can you confirm whether Redwood can provide a carve-out or a mechanism to opt specific data streams out (for both hosted and dedicated options)?

2) Subprocessors & transfers: we need a clear registry of subprocessors that might process EU customer data, and an explanation of how traffic is routed for EU accounts. Specifically: is there an SFTP/transfer path that keeps data within the EU/EAA, or do you rely on cross-border providers? We need to understand controls and, if applicable, standard contractual clauses/procurement artifacts.

3) Retention and export: our retention policy requires an exportable manifest of prompt/response pairs within 30 days of request. Does Redwood offer an automated export for transcripts tied to a customer project ID?

Can you route this to your privacy team and respond with a short checklist we can attach to our legal review? We can provide redline suggestions after that.

Thanks —
Olivia
Head of Product Operations
ClinicaHealth

--
Attachment: none in this message

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Park <olivia.park@clinicahealth.com>
Cc: Grace Oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 09:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: DPA: clarification on training consent, subprocessors and EU routing

Hi Olivia —

Appreciate the clear list. I've looped in Grace (privacy) and Dev (platform) — see answers below and attached artifacts. Short version: we can provide an opt-out for model improvement at the workspace/account level, and we have EU routing controls for customer projects pinned to EU regions. Details: 

- Training / model improvement: Redwood offers a "No-Model-Training" flag per project/account. When enabled, we do not use prompts/responses from that project for offline model improvement or research. This applies across Hosted API and Dedicated pools. It does not change runtime safety monitoring (e.g., abuse detection), but those telemetry events are pseudonymized and only used for security.

- Subprocessors & transfers: we maintain a subprocessors registry (attached excerpt) that lists infra and observability providers. For EU accounts we can pin compute, storage, and logging to EU-only subprocessors where available; fallback providers are documented. When you choose EU routing we provision project resources in our eu-central region and avoid cross-border storage. We will include SCC/SCC-equivalent artifacts where required.

- Retention/export: we support on-demand export of transcripts for a project via a secure SFTP endpoint or a one-click CSV export from the Console (sample mapping attached). Exports include timestamps, token counts, and metadata. We have a 30-day export SLA for production accounts under contract.

Next steps: we've attached two files (Redwood_DPA_excerpt_training_clause_v3.pdf and data_flow_map_clinica_sftp.xlsx) showing proposed DPA language and the export flow. Grace — can you confirm the final wording for the no-train clause and whether the export manifest satisfies their retention requirement?

Markus
Director, Partnerships — Redwood Inference

--
Attachments: Redwood_DPA_excerpt_training_clause_v3.pdf (PDF, 145KB), data_flow_map_clinica_sftp.xlsx (XLSX, 42KB)

From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@hjl-law.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Grace Oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Olivia Park <olivia.park@clinicahealth.com>, James Turner <j.turner@clinicahealth.com>
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 11:34:00 +0000
Subject: ClinicaHealth redlines and two follow-ups re: DPA wording

Markus / Grace —

We reviewed the excerpt. A few redline requests and two clarifying questions: 

A) Redline requests (high level):
- Replace "may be used" with explicit language that "Customer Data will not be used for model training or improvement without Customer's prior written consent," with an exception for security/abuse telemetry (that must be limited, pseudonymized, and not used for model training).
- Add an audit right for subprocessors handling EU data with 30 days' notice.

B) Clarifications: 
1) The no-train flag: is it reversible by an admin? If reversible, who at Redwood can toggle it and what logging/audit trails exist? We need assurance it's not manually overridden without customer authorization.
2) SFTP exports: the flow doc references a temporary staging bucket in a third-party cloud provider in the EU. Please confirm that staging is encrypted, access-controlled, and that keys are customer-segregated. Also, how long are files left in staging before permanent deletion?

We can produce a redline, but the answers to B1/B2 will determine which edits are acceptable.

Regards,
Elena Ruiz
Senior Counsel, HJL LLP (for ClinicaHealth)

--
Attachment: Clinica_redline_notes_v1.docx (referenced; not attached in this thread)

From: Grace Oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@hjl-law.com>, Olivia Park <olivia.park@clinicahealth.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 16:45:00 +0000
Subject: Re: ClinicaHealth redlines and two follow-ups re: DPA wording

Thanks Elena — good questions. Quick answers from privacy & platform: 

1) No-train flag: it is a customer-managed setting in Console and requires two-step org-admin approval to enable/disable (UI + API token confirmation). Any change is logged to our audit ledger with user id, timestamp, and request origin; logs are retained for 24 months and exportable. Manual overrides by Redwood personnel are not permitted without a written, auditable request from the customer (we can add an escalation workflow in the DPA if required).

2) SFTP / staging: staging buckets are provisioned in the EU region using provider contracts that support customer-specific encryption keys (KMS). Buckets are encrypted at rest, access is role-restricted, and object lifecycle rules delete staging files within 48 hours after successful export ingestion. We can include an explicit clause in the DPA about encryption, key segregation, and 48-hour max staging retention.

3) Subprocessor audits: we can agree to a 30-day notice audit right for subprocessors that process EU data; audits are subject to mutual NDAs and standard limitations. The subprocessors registry excerpt attached to Markus' message shows current providers and EU-specific alternatives.

Next steps: I'll incorporate these confirmations into a short DPA addendum for ClinicaHealth and share a DocuSign link for signature. Markus — share the HubSpot/deal link and I'll attach the addendum to the record.

Best,
Grace Oconnor
Senior Privacy Counsel — Redwood Inference
